notes: Pre-2010 lineage record. Steinbrecher (from the Ohio Valley Conference) has been the MAC's only commissioner for the entire 2010-2026 window - no MAC transitions in scope.

outgoing: Jim Isch (interim, after Myles Brand's death in Sept. 2009)
notes: Emmert hired from the University of Washington presidency (earlier LSU chancellor) - the classic academic-to-NCAA path.

outgoingDestination: Founded a consulting firm (The Beebe Group)
notes: Beebe (commissioner since 2007) was forced out by the board after losing Nebraska and Colorado (2010) and Texas A&M (2011) with Missouri wavering; Oklahoma's leadership pushed for his removal. Neinas, the Big 8's former commissioner and a coach-search consultant, served as interim while the league adopted equal revenue sharing and a six-year grant of rights.

Marinatto (commissioner since July 2009, succeeding Mike Tranghese) resigned under pressure after Pittsburgh and Syracuse (ACC, Sept. 2011), West Virginia (Big 12) and TCU (Big 12, before ever playing a Big East game) left; the league had reportedly rejected a ~$1B+ ESPN extension in 2011.
Bowlsby hired from the Stanford AD chair (previously Iowa AD); classic former-AD hire. Served 2012-2022.
Waters had led the Sun Belt since 1998. Benson was poached from the WAC (commissioner since 1994) as the WAC's FBS football collapsed.
Last FBS-era WAC transition; the WAC dropped FBS football after 2012.

Aresco hired from CBS Sports (EVP programming) in Aug. 2012 - an early media-exec hire. When the seven Catholic non-FBS schools split in 2013 and took the Big East name, Aresco stayed with the football schools, whose charter became the American Athletic Conference.

Founding commissioner of the re-formed (basketball) Big East built by the 'Catholic 7' plus Butler, Creighton and Xavier, with a 12-year Fox deal. Ackerman was founding WNBA president (1996-2005) and USA Basketball president; she had just written an NCAA report on women's basketball. Tranghese -> Marinatto (2009) -> Aresco (2012) is the old-Big East lineage.

Slive (SEC 2002-2015; earlier C-USA founding commissioner) announced retirement in Oct. 2014 while battling cancer. SEC presidents promoted his COO/executive associate commissioner Sankey - the textbook internal-succession hire. Exact date of the presidents' selection not verified; 2015-06-01 is Sankey's start.

outgoingDestination: Executive director, College Football Playoff Foundation
notes: Banowsky (C-USA commissioner since 2002) announced his departure July 16, 2015. MacLeod, the league's COO, was named interim Aug. 17, 2015 and permanent Oct. 26, 2015 - first woman to lead an FBS conference.
Gill hired from the Atlantic 10 staff (ex-Richmond AD); first Black commissioner of an FBS conference.

outgoingDestination: Retirement; Big Ten consulting (FY2024-25 990: $5.82M in bonuses/deferred comp plus $600K consulting fees)
notes: Delany (commissioner since 1989) built BTN and the 2010-14 expansion. Warren, Minnesota Vikings COO (Notre Dame J.D.), became the first Black Power Five commissioner. His 2020 postponement/reversal of the football season was the defining controversy of his tenure.

outgoingDestination: Retirement (ACC paid him ~$2.6M in 2022, largely deferred compensation)
notes: Swofford led the ACC 1997-2021 (expansion to Miami/VT/BC, then Pitt/Syracuse/Louisville/ND, the 20-year ESPN deal and ACC Network). Search began Aug. 2020, facilitated by Turnkey Search; Clemson president Jim Clements was the presumptive favorite until Clemson's board kept him. Phillips was Northwestern AD.

Scott (2009-2021; ex-WTA CEO) agreed in Jan. 2021 to leave June 30, 2021 amid criticism of the Pac-12 Network's poor distribution, lavish spending and lagging revenue; reported ~$1.5M severance. Kliavkoff (MGM Resorts president of entertainment & sports) chosen unanimously after a ~4-month global search (200+ candidates) by the executive committee (chair: Oregon's Michael Schill) and TurnkeyZRG; five-year contract.

outgoingDestination: Stepped away; six months of consulting for the Big 12
notes: Bowlsby's final-year payout totaled ~$17.2M: $12.26M for the three years left on his contract, $3.337M vested deferred comp, $15K consulting. Big 12 retained TurnkeyZRG (RFP to several firms) on 2022-04-21; executive committee (Texas Tech's Lawrence Schovanec, Baylor's Linda Livingstone, Kansas's Doug Girod) led it. Yormark (Roc Nation, ex-Nets CEO) got a five-year deal.

Emmert's exit was announced April 2022 (mutual agreement; contract had been extended through 2025 in 2021). Board of Governors subcommittee chaired by Baylor's Linda Livingstone ran the search with TurnkeyZRG (Len Perna), after interviewing 300+ stakeholders; hired the outgoing Massachusetts governor.

Thompson was the MWC's founding commissioner (1998-2022) and announced retirement Sept. 2022. Nevarez poached from the WCC. A search firm approached her; Parker Executive Search lists the placement on its site (attribution likely but unconfirmed).
Non-FBS but shows the lateral-promotion chain (WCC -> MWC). Jackson hired from the Big East staff (ex-NBA EVP).

Bears announced Warren in Jan. 2023; his Big Ten tenure ended 2023-04-14. He collected a $5.75M media-rights bonus for the 2022 Fox/CBS/NBC deal (total $6.83M in the year). Search led by the COPC Executive Search Committee (chair: Maryland's Darryll Pines) with TurnkeyZRG; ACC's Jim Phillips was a reported target and took an ACC extension instead.

Mutual separation announced mid-Feb. 2024 (reports Feb. 9-13); Kliavkoff's last day 2024-02-29; financial terms undisclosed at the time, but the Pac-12's later 990 showed $6.1M paid to him in 2024, $5M of it severance ($15.6M over his tenure) - effectively a contract buyout negotiated as a settlement. The two-member board (WSU's Kirk Schulz as chair, OSU's Jayathi Murthy) announced deputy commissioner Gould on 2024-02-19, effective March 1, on a two-year deal. Context: his Aug. 2023 Apple streaming pitch preceded the exit of eight schools in days, leaving only OSU and WSU.

Aresco (Big East football 2012-13, American 2013-24) announced retirement in Dec. 2023. The AAC board voted unanimously for Pernetti (IMG Academy president, ex-Rutgers AD, ex-CBS) after a search led by the board executive committee (chair: ECU's Philip Rogers) with TurnkeyZRG. Brief's '2023' date is the retirement announcement, not the hire.
Hancock (ex-Big 8/Big 12 staff, NCAA Final Four director, BCS administrator, CFP executive director since 2012) retired; Rich Clark succeeded him. Clark's prior role not verified in this pass.
McGlade (A-10 since 2008) announced 2025-11-19 she would retire after 2025-26. Leibovitz hired from the Big East (senior associate commissioner, MBB).

Ackerman announced 2026-04-20 she would retire Aug. 31, 2026 after 13 years. Brosnan (Georgetown alum, 24 years at MLB incl. CEO of MLB Enterprises) named sixth commissioner; search emphasized revenue generation.

outgoingDestination: Executive director, Collegiate Women Sports Awards
notes: Morris led the NEC 16 years; announced April 2026. Permanent successor not named as of Nov. 2026.

outgoingDestination: CEO, Milan Sports & Entertainment (RedBird Capital-backed holding company, Milan)
notes: Announced 2026-10-30, ~18 months after a May 2025 extension through 2030 - i.e., walked away from three-plus years.
